The Charter is Baltimore's governing document, often described as the City's constitution. Browse by article below, or use the search box in the left menu to find a word or phrase, such as "lowest bidder" or "Board of Estimates".

## The 2026 ballot questions and the charter

This copy of the charter is current through October 1, 2026, so it does not yet include the amendments from the November 3, 2026 election. These are the places in the charter that we have confirmed the questions change:

- **Question E (contract bidding):** [Article VI](article-vi.html#s-11), § 11, which covers bid awards, tie bids and bonds. Those rules are removed on November 7, 2028 unless the city replaces them sooner. [Read the guide](../elections/2026/general/index.qmd#question-baltimore-e).

- **Question F (budget, vetoes and the Board of Estimates):** [Article III](article-iii.html#s-15) § 15, [Article IV](article-iv.html#s-5) § 5, and the budget and Board of Estimates sections of [Article VI](article-vi.html). Most changes start December 3, 2026. [Read the guide](../elections/2026/general/index.qmd#question-baltimore-f).

The exact wording of the amendments is in the [State Board of Elections amendment text (PDF)](https://elections.maryland.gov/elections/2026/Baltimore_City_Proposed_Charter_Amendment_Text.pdf). Section references for Questions G, H and I are not listed here yet.
